newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yeltsin says Russia should join Paris club.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Russia should join Paris club.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Thursday that he expected Moscow to be admitted to the Paris club of sovereign lenders this year.
"I think that we should join the Paris club already in the current year," Yeltsin told a news conference after a meeting here with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
Yeltsin says Russia should join Paris club
Germany and Russia in February signed a pact to reschedule 25 billion marks in debts owed by the defunct Soviet Union for 20 to 25 years.
The deal was hailed at the time by German officials as the last outstanding deal governing debts owed to Germany -- which account for half of Russia's foreign debt.
The debt agreement represented the bilateral implementation of a Paris club deal reached a year ago, and Waigel said it opened the way for Russia to tap international capital markets again.
Moscow late last year issued a $1 billion Eurobond, and also issued two billion mark bond in March. Bankers expect it to return to the market with a second dollar offering in June.
